title: Why Hotel Hallways Always Look the Same
titleZh: 酒店走廊，全世界最大的密室
summary:
放眼全球，无论身处何地，只要入住大型连锁酒店，其走廊设计几乎都如出一辙。只要住过一次，这样的画面便不难想象：沉闷乏味的花纹地毯、一眼望不到头且几乎完全相同的排排房门，沿途可能还零星点缀着不起眼的装饰画或镜子。沿走廊前行，在某些楼层的角落，你会看到一间小房间，里面摆放着自动售货机和制冰机；再往前是电梯间，继续走下去，则是通往楼梯的安全门。置身于这种由无尽重复的布局、令人眩晕的图案和一道道紧锁房门交织而成的迷宫中，有时确实容易让人迷失方向。如果你也曾好奇这一切背后的缘由，这里有几个基础的解释。

来源：MentalFloss；作者：Eden Gordon；原文发布时间：2026-04-30 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: No matter where you are in the world, if you’re staying in any sort of large hotel chain, the hallways are likely to look almost exactly the same. It’s easy to picture if you’ve been to even one: dreary patterned carpet, an endless series of nearly identical doors, and perhaps some unassuming art or mirrors along the way. At one point, on some floors, there’ll be a little room with a vending machine and an ice-maker; at another point you’ll reach the elevator, and at another you’ll find the door to the stairs. It’s sometimes all too easy to get lost in this mazelike vortex of endless repetition, dizzying patterns, and locked doors. If you've ever wondered about the reasons behind all this, there are a few basic explanations.
paragraphs.contentZh: 放眼全球，无论身处何地，只要入住大型连锁酒店，其走廊设计几乎都如出一辙。只要住过一次，这样的画面便不难想象：沉闷乏味的花纹地毯、一眼望不到头且几乎完全相同的排排房门，沿途可能还零星点缀着不起眼的装饰画或镜子。沿走廊前行，在某些楼层的角落，你会看到一间小房间，里面摆放着自动售货机和制冰机；再往前是电梯间，继续走下去，则是通往楼梯的安全门。置身于这种由无尽重复的布局、令人眩晕的图案和一道道紧锁房门交织而成的迷宫中，有时确实容易让人迷失方向。如果你也曾好奇这一切背后的缘由，这里有几个基础的解释。

paragraphs.contentEn: First and foremost, hotel design is always intended to maximize guests' comfort, happiness, and willingness to book more stays in the future. While it may not seem completely intuitive that a completely recognizable hallway setup would equal guest satisfaction, seeing a repetitive, familiar layout “reinforces brand loyalty and trust,” according to the architecture magazine ArchUp. This plays into the same psychology that makes us reach for familiar brands even if cheaper options might be available. Humans associate familiarity with safety and reliability, and prevailing wisdom holds that exhausted travelers are more likely to be grateful for comfort than novelty.
paragraphs.contentZh: 首先，酒店设计的首要目标，始终是最大程度提升住客的舒适感、满意度，以及他们未来复订的意愿。尽管乍看之下，高度统一且极易辨识的走廊布局似乎与入住体验并无直接关联，但据建筑杂志《ArchUp》指出，这种重复的熟悉感实际上“会强化品牌忠诚与信任”。这一设计迎合的，是一种普遍的消费心理：即便存在更廉价的替代选择，人们仍倾向于选择熟悉的品牌。对大多数人来说，熟悉即意味着安全与可靠，同时一种广为接受的看法是，相比新鲜感，长途奔波后的旅客更渴望安稳的舒适体验。

paragraphs.contentEn: Even the art on hotel hallway walls is typically intentionally inoffensive and abstract in order to “avoid cultural sensitivity issues,” per ArchUp. Neutral wall color palettes can also trigger associations with cleanliness and a sense of calm. Predictable layouts also make it easier for guests to find ice-makers, exits, and elevators. Sound also plays a role in hotel hallway design, as thick carpets help muffle the sound of late-night arrivals and disruptive conversations.
paragraphs.contentZh: 《ArchUp》杂志指出，即便是酒店走廊墙上的装饰画，通常也会特意选用温和无害、风格抽象的作品，以“避免触及文化敏感问题”。中性色调的墙面也能让人联想到洁净，并传递出宁静感。模式化的空间布局则让住客能更轻易地找到制冰机、出口和电梯。除此之外，声音同样是设计考量的一部分，厚实的地毯有助于减弱深夜入住时的声响，降低打扰他人的谈话音量。

paragraphs.contentEn: Sometimes, hotels’ identical hallways also have underlying economic reasons behind them. Many hotel chains utilize the same building techniques and materials all across the world, which cuts costs and can lead to standardization. Also, hotel rooms tend to be placed close to each other and in specific arrangements so they can share plumbing infrastructure.
paragraphs.contentZh: 有时，酒店千篇一律的走廊背后，也暗藏着经济层面的原因。许多连锁酒店在全球范围内采用统一的建造工艺和材料，在降低成本的同时，也推动了整体设计的标准化。此外，酒店客房往往排列紧凑、布局规整，以便共享管网等基础设施。

paragraphs.contentEn: Most hotel hallways are also designed to maximize space and costs while preserving guest comfort. They’re typically 60 to 72 inches wide, a size that can accommodate two service carts next to each other and that can allow a suitcase to pass a service cart, but not too much more. Additionally, in the United States, the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) generally requires public spaces to be a minimum width of 60 inches so that two wheelchairs can pass one another.
paragraphs.contentZh: 大多数酒店走廊的设计也致力于在兼顾住客舒适的前提下，尽可能优化空间利用和成本效益。走廊宽度通常控制在60至72英寸之间，这一尺寸既能容纳两辆服务车并排停放，也允许拖着行李箱的客人从服务车旁通过，但空间余量并不多。此外，在美国，《美国残疾人法案》（ADA）一般要求公共空间的最小宽度为60英寸，以确保两台轮椅能够顺利交会通行。

paragraphs.contentEn: Additionally, the carpets we see in hotel hallways are often anything but calming, and sometimes the patterns can get a bit out of hand, particularly in older hotel chains. This actually has more to do with cleanliness than anything else, as a busy pattern better disguises stains and dirt and makes cleaning less of an urgent task for hotel staff.
paragraphs.contentZh: 除此之外，酒店走廊铺设的地毯在视觉上往往很难带来平静感，尤其是在部分老牌连锁酒店中，图案有时甚至显得过于繁复。但事实上，这种设计最根本的考量在于耐脏，花哨的图案能更好地掩盖污渍和灰尘，从而减轻保洁人员随时随地需要清洁的压力。

paragraphs.contentEn: Of course, all this is not necessarily the case for many boutique, luxury, or locally-owned hotels. Recent years have seen an overarching shift from standardized, globalized hotel templates to unique designs based more on local cultures and individual locations. While some people might enjoy standard hotels' traditionally similar appearances, for others, hotel hallways can feel like uncanny liminal spaces, particularly when they’re extremely quiet and empty. If identical hotel hallways give you the heebie jeebies and make you feel like you're in The Shining rather than on vacation, there’s always the option of a locally owned, reliably quirky bed and breakfast.
paragraphs.contentZh: 当然，上述这些情况对许多精品酒店、高端奢华酒店或本地人经营的酒店来说未必如此。近年来，酒店业整体出现了一种从标准化、全球化的酒店模板，转向更依托在地文化和具体地点进行独特设计的趋势。虽然有人偏爱连锁酒店那种传统统一的风格，但在另一些人看来，这类走廊会营造出一种令人不安的阈限空间感，尤其是当走廊极为安静又空无一人时。如果千篇一律的走廊让你感到心里发毛，觉得自己仿佛置身《闪灵》的片场，而不是在度假，那么，选择一家由当地人经营、风格奇趣的民宿，或许会是不错的替代方案。
